page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 family. It features 2 vCPUs and 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1399.29 falls into the bottom 25%, while the multi-core score of 1841.88 is in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers measured at 13.72 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.78 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10%. Similarly, the Geekbench multi-core score of 1311.0 and Passmark CPU score of 2160.18 reflect constrained processing capacity under multi-threaded workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-2 serves as a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources. However, the low resource density, specifically the 2.0 GB memory limit, presents a significant tradeoff, restricting its utility for memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for lightweight, compute-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory, such as basic single-threaded processing, simple text processing, or lightweight static web serving.
